title: Criteria available on ZPA access policy rules

prose.text: A rule matches only when its criteria all match, and the criteria have limits on how they combine.

prose.label: Spellings.
prose.text: The client type names differ between the help and the wire {{divergence:client-type-names}}. The platform list differs too {{divergence:platform-values}}.

prose.label: Combination limits.
prose.text: Web Browser rules cannot use posture or trusted network criteria: [[zpa.browser-access.policy:no-posture-with-web-browser]]. {{cloud-connector-groups-exclude-saml}} A machine group needs the Machine Tunnel client type: [[zpa.machine-groups.policy-use:console-pairs-client-type]]. {{gap:workload-group-cloud-connector-client-type}}

prose.label: On the global rules and policy groups page.
prose.text: The page for those rules, whose feature is in limited availability [[zpa.policy.policy-groups:limited-availability]], adds these criteria limits. {{adaptive-access-profile-selection}} {{adaptive-access-client-types}} {{adaptive-access-exclusions}} {{cloud-connector-groups-exclude-adaptive}} {{workload-group-needs-cloud-connector}} {{global-rules-no-posture-web-browser}}

prose.label: Country.
prose.text: {{country-last-nat-ip}} Browser Access and PRA do not support it: [[zpa.browser-access.policy:country-codes-unsupported]].

prose.label: Identity criteria.
prose.text: {{nameid-unsupported}} {{idp-policy-setting-disabled}} Timing of SCIM data is in [[zpa.policy.scim-sync]].

prose.label: Federated and Chrome.
prose.text: The guest partner criteria are in [[zpa.b2b-federation.access-policy:guest-criteria-limited]]. {{chrome-posture-profile-sub-option}}
The AND and OR logic is in [[zpa.policy.conditions]].

checks.do: Which criteria the rule uses, and whether the request must match every one of them.
If the rule is scoped on application segments, remember that a rule may name individual segments as well as segment groups.

If a country criterion is used with Source IP Anchoring, Cloud Connector or multi-hop traffic, check which public IP the country is derived from, and that the application is not Browser Access or PRA.
If a rule has SAML or SCIM criteria, check the IdP's SAML Attributes for Policy and SCIM Attributes and Groups for Policy settings.
If a rule seems unable to combine two criteria, check the combinations the help rules out.
If a rule uses Adaptive Access Profiles, check its client types and that it does not also use the criteria the global rules page rules out.
When matching a client type or platform name between the console and an export, compare all the spellings the sources use.

criteria-list.statement: The help lists these access policy criteria: Adaptive Access Profiles, Applications, Branch Connector Groups, Chrome Enterprise Browser, Client Connector Posture Profiles, Client Connector Trusted Networks, Client Types, Cloud Connector Groups, Country Codes, Extranet, Federated Applications, Locations, Machine Groups, Platforms, Risk Scores, SAML Attributes, SCIM Attributes, SCIM Groups, Segment Groups, Tag Groups, Tag Value and Workload Groups.

quotes: Adaptive Access Profiles: The profiles defined by user and device context signals from the Adaptive Access Engine.
Applications: A grouping of defined applications based upon access type or user privileges.
Branch Connector Groups: The group of Branch Connectors to which the policy applies.
Chrome Enterprise Browser: Verify if the users are accessing private applications by using the Chrome Enterprise browser.
Client Connector Posture Profiles: Zscaler Client Connector device posture profiles are the set of criteria that a user's device must meet
Client Connector Trusted Networks: The type of network the user is connected to that Zscaler Client Connector can trust.
Client Types: The available client types are
Cloud Connector Groups: The group of Cloud Connectors to which the policy applies.
Country Codes: The country that a user's IP address is located in.
Extranet: The extranet resources (i.e., extranet locations or extranet sublocations).
Federated Applications: The defined application segments that are created, owned, and managed by the host partner
Locations: The Branch Connector, Cloud Connector, or other locations and sublocations.
Machine Groups: The group of configured machines.
Platforms: The user devices to which the policy applies.
Risk Scores: User risk scores from a risk source
SAML Attributes: User attributes obtained from the SAML assertion from an IdP.
SCIM Attributes: User attributes learned via SCIM from an IdP.
SCIM Groups: SCIM groups learned via SCIM from an IdP.
Segment Groups: The group of configured application segments.
Tag Groups: The tags associated with the tag group defined within the application segment.
Tag Value: The values associated with configured application segments.
Workload Groups: The Workload Groups from your cloud workloads.

all-criteria-must-match.statement: A user's application request must match all the conditions within a policy rule.

quotes: A user's application request must match all the conditions within a policy rule.

application-segments-criterion.statement: A rule can include individual application segments as well as segment groups: segments are used to apply different policies to individual applications, and segment groups to give a set of users similar access across many applications.

quotes: When you need to apply different policies to individual applications, create an access policy rule that includes one or more application segments.
if you want all applications within a group of users who need a similar level of access across those applications, create an access policy rule that includes one or more segment groups.
| `APP` | Application segments | Application segment IDs |

country-last-nat-ip.statement: For Cloud Connectors, Source IP Anchoring traffic and Private Access multi-hop, the country criterion uses the last NATed layer 3 public IP address, so SIPA traffic takes its country from the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edge's public IP.

quotes: In the case of Cloud Connectors, Source IP Anchoring traffic, or Private Access multi-hop, Private Access country criteria policy is applied using the last NATed layer 3 public IP address.
For example, SIPA traffic identifies the country based on the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edge’s public IP address.

cloud-connector-groups-exclude-saml.statement: The Cloud Connector Groups criteria cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria.

quotes: The Cloud Connector Groups criteria cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria.

chrome-posture-profile-sub-option.statement: The help presents the Chrome posture profile as an option under Chrome Enterprise Browser, while the Terraform provider validates it as the separate object type CHROME_POSTURE_PROFILE.

quotes: Enable Chrome Enterprise Browser to verify that users are accessing private applications via the Chrome Enterprise browser.
When enabled, you can also select a configured Chrome posture profile to evaluate criteria for access to private applications.
case "CHROME_POSTURE_PROFILE":

idp-policy-setting-disabled.statement: If the IdP's SAML Attributes for Policy (or SCIM Attributes and Groups for Policy) setting is disabled but a rule has criteria of that kind, an OR operator skips those criteria and evaluates the other kind, while an AND operator makes Private Access not evaluate the rule at all.

quotes: OR: Private Access skips evaluating the criteria for SAML attributes, but continues to evaluate the criteria for SCIM attributes and SCIM groups.
AND: Private Access does not evaluate this policy rule. You must remove the criteria under SAML Attributes for Private Access to process the policy rule.
OR: Private Access skips evaluating the criteria for SCIM attributes and SCIM groups, but continues to evaluate the criteria for SAML attributes.
AND: Private Access does not evaluate this policy rule. You must remove the criteria for SCIM attributes and SCIM groups for Private Access to process the policy rule.

nameid-unsupported.statement: Using the SAML NameID as a SAML attribute within access and timeout policy rules is not supported; the same value can be used by defining it as a user attribute.

quotes: Using NameID as a SAML attribute within access and timeout policy rules is not supported.
However, you can use the value associated with NameID within your policy rule criteria by explicitly defining a user attribute

risk-score-values-call.statement: The Go SDK reads the valid risk score values from `GET .../riskScoreValues`, with an optional `excludeUnknown` flag.

quotes: func GetRiskScoreValues(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, excludeUnknown *bool) ([]string, *http.Response, error) {
relativeURL := mgmtConfigV2 + service.Client.GetCustomerID() + "/riskScoreValues"
if excludeUnknown != nil { relativeURL = fmt.Sprintf("%s?excludeUnknown=%t", relativeURL, *excludeUnknown) }
resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "GET", relativeURL, common.Filter{MicroTenantID: service.MicroTenantID()}, nil, &result)

adaptive-access-profile-selection.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page there is no limit to the number of adaptive access profiles that can be selected, and multiple profiles within a rule are joined by an OR Boolean operator by default, which can be toggled to AND.

quotes: Choose the adaptive access profiles to which the rule applies. There is no limit to the number you can select. Click More Profiles to include additional profiles.
If you added multiple profiles within a rule, Private Access uses an OR Boolean operator between them by default. However, you can toggle this to an AND operator by clicking on it.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

adaptive-access-client-types.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the Adaptive Access Profile criteria is only supported with the Client Connector, Client Connector Partner, Cloud Browser, or Web Browser client types.

quotes: Additionally, the Adaptive Access Profile criteria is only supported with the Client Connector, Client Connector Partner, Cloud Browser, or Web Browser client types.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

adaptive-access-exclusions.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the Adaptive Access Profiles criteria cannot be configured with the Branch Connector Groups, Cloud Connector Groups, Locations, and Machine Groups criteria.

quotes: The Adaptive Access Profiles criteria cannot be configured with the Branch Connector Groups, Cloud Connector Groups, Locations, and Machine Groups criteria.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

cloud-connector-groups-exclude-adaptive.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the Cloud Connector Group criteria type cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes or Adaptive Access Profiles criteria.

quotes: The Cloud Connector Group criteria type cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes or Adaptive Access Profiles criteria.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

workload-group-needs-cloud-connector.statement: In the policy group instructions of the global rules and policy groups configuration page, a specific workload group is chosen from the drop-down menu to apply the rule action to, and if Workload Group is selected, Cloud Connector as a client type is required; a limited availability notice precedes the item.

quotes: This feature is in limited availability. Contact Zscaler Support to learn more.
Choose a specific workload group from the drop-down menu to apply the rule action to.
If Workload Group is selected, Cloud Connector as a client type is required.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Policy Groups

global-rules-no-posture-web-browser.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page, rules using the Web Browser or ZIA Service Edge client types additionally can't use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria.

quotes: Rules using the Web Browser or ZIA Service Edge client types additionally can't use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

external-iam-idp-criterion.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the External IAM IdPs criteria is the external IdP attribute configured in Authentication Service and is only supported for IdPs created in Authentication Service.

quotes: External IAM IdPs
This criteria is the external IdP attribute configured in Authentication Service and is only supported for IdPs created in Authentication Service.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

extranet-location-criterion.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the Extranet Location criteria chooses the extranet resource, extranet locations, and extranet location groups to which the policy rule applies; the locations and groups fields are only visible after an extranet resource is selected, and the criteria is not visible within a Microtenant.

quotes: Choose the extranet resource, extranet locations, and extranet location groups to which the policy rule applies.
Select a location from the Extranet Locations drop-down menu. This field is only visible after an extranet resource is selected.
Select a group from the Extranet Location Groups drop-down menu. This field is only visible after an extranet resource is selected.
The Extranet Location criteria is not visible if you are within a Microtenant.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

locations-types.statement: On the global rules and policy groups configuration page the Locations criteria lists the location types BC (Branch Connector), CC (Cloud Connector) and NONE (locations other than Branch Connector or Cloud Connector), where NONE location types are also used in Source IP Anchoring configurations in which traffic is routed from these locations to Private Access.

quotes: BC - Branch Connector
CC - Cloud Connector

NONE - Locations other than Branch Connector or Cloud Connector. NONE location types are also used in Source IP Anchoring configurations, where traffic is routed from these locations to Private Access.
evidence.after: Configure an Access Policy for Global Rules

positions.says: The global rules and policy groups page lists eight client types: Client Connector, Client Connector Partner, Cloud Browser, Cloud Connector, Branch Connector, Machine Tunnel, Web Browser and ZIA Service Edge, so like the Configuring Access Policies article it includes Cloud Browser and names the service edge type ZIA Service Edge.

quotes: | `CLIENT_TYPE` | Client connector type | `zpn_client_type_zapp`, `zpn_client_type_exporter`, `zpn_client_type_machine_tunnel`, `zpn_client_type_browser_isolation`, `zpn_client_type_ip_anchoring`, `zpn_client_type_edge_connector`, `zpn_client_type_branch_connector`, `zpn_client_type_zapp_partner` |

positions.says: The wire values are zpn_client_type_* strings. Pairing browser_isolation, ip_anchoring and edge_connector with the console's Cloud Browser, service edge and Cloud Connector is an inference; no source states the mapping.

client-type-names.impact: A rule exported from the API cannot be matched to console wording by name alone, and the two articles disagree on whether Cloud Browser is a type.

quotes: - Windows - macOS - Linux - iOS - Android
| `PLATFORM` | `linux`, `android`, `ios`, `mac`, `windows` | `"true"` or `"false"` |

platform-values.impact: Whether iOS can be targeted by a Platforms criterion depends on which article is read.

workload-group-cloud-connector-client-ty.title: Whether selecting a Workload Group requires Cloud Connector as a client type outside the global rules and policy groups page
workload-group-cloud-connector-client-ty.blocks: the client-type requirement for rules that use Workload Group criteria on the access policy page
workload-group-cloud-connector-client-ty.detail: Partly answered: the global rules and policy groups configuration page, a limited-availability feature, says that if Workload Group is selected, Cloud Connector as a client type is required (claim workload-group-needs-cloud-connector). The legacy statement "If a Workload Group is selected, Cloud Connector is required as a client type" was previously sourced from Configuring_Access_Policies.txt (PDF text). The recapture (configuring-access-policies.json) has no Workload Group client-type rule, and zpa-access-policy-20260909.json lists Workload Groups only as a criterion.
